about: The area config for the cross-feature round (#8005 slice 4): goals that cross features — the front page and its windows, placing a paper order, research and the automated strategies, a bot's page, the league, and the chat assistant in every member's hands. Read by scripts/study/round.mjs; the world is scripts/study/worlds/cross-today.mjs (Thursday 2026-11-19, the profile league moved six weeks). Phone first: every member is on a phone but the first-timer, whose card puts them on a laptop; the owner has a desktop pairing too. Every member starts on the front page, the app's entry point. `roles` is who each member is here, in plain words, never a card's (#5099). The framer and the task author write the tasks later, blind.

matrix.note: a non-owner: their own small account, the league, and the owner's bot by the app's own links

roles.eric: Runs the league and the automated accounts in it. Checks the whole picture daily, mostly on a phone between other things, at a desk when there is time.
roles.returning-trader: Holds one paper account and knows the trading words, and is back after a few weeks away to act on something they hold. On a phone this time.
roles.bot-watcher: Places few trades; follows the automated accounts and the standings the way a fan follows a season. On a phone.
roles.phone-only: Uses the app only on a phone, with one hand, a few minutes at a time.
roles.invited-friend: Was invited by the owner; has a small account of their own and comes to see it and how the league is going. On a phone.
roles.first-timer: Signed in for the first time today, with no account linked and nothing of their own in the app yet. On a laptop.

pages: the front page: the day's market news, a box to ask a question, and short paths to explore
the front page's views: the whole market by sector, a calendar of stories and reports, suggested next moves for your account, and how everyone in the league is doing
the page for placing a paper order on one stock or option, with its chart, its options, advice about a holding, and a list of names to watch
your accounts: what everything is worth, what you hold, and your history
research: the house's notes and calls, how each market sector is covered, the automated strategies a bot can run, and your own views on a stock
a bot account's own page: how it is doing, what it did, the strategies it runs and its reasoning
the league: a ranking of every account, and a feed of everyone's trades
a chat assistant on every page that answers questions, takes you to a page, and can write up a request to change the app for you to send
